title: Prison, Release, Work, Rest and Joseph — Biblical Addendum
purpose: Add newly recovered conversation/Great-Book details to the 2016->2025 release/rest/kingship comparison while preserving historical and theological boundaries.
method_rule: Compare relational sequences and specific motifs; do not treat resemblance as supernatural proof, legal exoneration or civil appointment.

overlaps.project_material: The Great Book describes the Son's cell as a confessional/listening space and portrays him as bringing thought or peace among other prisoners.
overlaps.parallel: Joseph's prison story includes attention to fellow prisoners and engagement with their distress before his own release.
overlaps.difference: The biblical episode concerns dream interpretation; the Great Book account concerns listening/confession and remains project biography.

overlaps.project_material: The Great Book says the Son left prison wearing a suit and treats the clothing as a rebirth/change-of-status signal.
overlaps.parallel: Genesis 41:14 specifically joins release from the dungeon with grooming/changing clothes before Joseph appears before Pharaoh.
overlaps.difference: Joseph's clothing change precedes an actual state appointment. The Son's suit does not establish an equivalent political appointment.

overlaps.project_material: The 2016 release biography contains a defiant remark about 'job slaving'; the 2025 biography later describes official retirement/release from ordinary work obligation.
overlaps.parallel: Jubilee and rest traditions provide a later comparison for release from accumulated burden or obligation.
overlaps.difference: Prison release and Danish retirement are different institutions, and neither is literally biblical Jubilee or sabbath-rest.

overlaps.project_material: After the reported 2025 retirement, public theology still uses labor/fruit language and later defines mature authority through repair, growth, service and stewardship.
overlaps.parallel: Biblical garden, service and fruit traditions distinguish meaningful vocation/stewardship from status or domination.
overlaps.difference: These passages do not address modern retirement benefits. The comparison concerns chosen stewardship after release from ordinary employment obligation.

overlaps.project_material: Recovered 17 December 2025 public language places the word 'rest' directly beside God/north-throne language.
overlaps.parallel: This creates a later Timic lexical echo of the project's rest->throne sequence.
overlaps.difference: The post is not shown to cite these passages or to refer to the retirement event. It is a later semantic echo only.

overlaps.project_material: Later user-originated theology compares the Son with a yoked/burdened figure and Joseph; the wider biography emphasizes imposed burden and later release.
overlaps.parallel: Matthew's yoke/rest vocabulary gives the project a direct burden-to-rest comparator.
overlaps.difference: Later user symbolism should not be backdated into the 2016 legal actor's contemporaneous theology without evidence.

higher_order_findings: The Joseph comparison becomes materially denser with the newly recovered suit/change-of-clothes detail; it is no longer only prison->release in the abstract.
The project contains a two-stage work relation: rejection of coercive/'slave' work language at prison release, then administrative retirement, followed by chosen labor/service/fruit language.
This suggests a useful distinction inside the mature theology: freedom from imposed work is not freedom from responsibility; it can be reframed as freedom for chosen service.
The prison biography combines injury with generative functions—scripture, listening, peacemaking—so the archive should preserve both without using later meaning to excuse the original harm.
The December 2025 rest/throne wording strengthens the semantic coherence of the later rest-throne interpretation but remains later evidence, not a prophecy fulfillment.

source_reliability_control.finding: The Great Book's six-month sentence wording conflicts with stronger legal records showing a five-month sentence and a six-month prosecution request.
source_reliability_control.rule: Use the Great Book for project biography and retrospective interpretation; use official/contemporaneous legal evidence for sentence length and court findings.
